# Refactor Plan: `WorkflowExecutionProcessor.py`

Target: `packages/syn-domain/src/syn_domain/contexts/orchestration/slices/execute_workflow/WorkflowExecutionProcessor.py`
(896 lines, threshold 750). Plan only — no code or test modified.

## 0. Governing input: coverage-gate verdict

The coverage gate returned **SAFE TO REFACTOR** (96% combined statement+branch
coverage, tests assert exact state rather than absence-of-exception, one
dedicated race test for the module's highest-risk concurrency behaviour). Per
the brief, that verdict shrinks this job — I am not specifying a
characterization suite to earn the right to refactor. I'm doing three
narrower things:

1. Naming the behaviours the gate flagged as *incidentally* pinned (covered
   by accident of what a handful of tests happen to exercise, not by design)
   that an extraction could silently lose.
2. Specifying the small, targeted tests that close each of those gaps —
   each one gates a specific extraction step, not "do them all first."
3. Sequencing the decomposition itself, and marking which parts of the
   target structure are moved code (characterization-covered) vs new code
   (TDD-covered).

Every step below assumes the full existing suite (5 files, `test_workflow_
execution_processor.py`, `test_removed_provider_execution.py`,
`test_processor_smoke.py`, `test_1036_failed_phase_duration.py`,
`test_capture_before_teardown.py`) stays green throughout — that suite *is*
the safety net for the moved code, per the gate's own read of it. A step is
not done until that suite plus its own gating test(s) are green.

## 1. What the module currently owns

Read end to end (896 lines). Five responsibilities, currently fused into one
class:

| Responsibility | Lines | Size |
|---|---|---|
| DI / construction, 16 collaborators + 10 ephemeral per-phase/per-execution state dicts | 127–201 | 75 |
| Top-level `run()` orchestration + to-do drain loop + action dispatch | 202–380 | 179 |
| Terminal outcomes: cancel / complete / fail, and shared workspace-CM teardown | 382–521 | 140 |
| Per-action handlers: PROVISION_WORKSPACE, RUN_AGENT (+ cancel-signal sub-path), COLLECT_ARTIFACTS, COMPLETE_PHASE (+ finalize) | 523–849 | 327 |
| Event persistence + projection sync: two near-duplicate save/sync loops, event serialization, event-type→handler-name mapping | 851–896 | 46 |

The dispatch loop and the four `_handle_*` happy paths are the parts doing
real orchestration — the coverage gate confirms none of the six coverage
gaps sit there. The gaps sit in edge branches of already-tested functions
and in the persistence duplication. That maps directly onto where this plan
puts its gating tests: not on the well-tested core, but on the four named
edge branches plus the duplication.

## 2. Behaviours pinned only incidentally — name them before touching anything

These are real, currently-true behaviours of the shipped code. None are
specified anywhere except by the fact that a test happens to reach them (or,
in three cases, that *no* test reaches them and the gate's own report is the
only record of the gap). Each entry says which extraction step it gates.

### 2.1 `_get_agent_handler`'s production construction path (line 618)

**Behaviour:** when `agent_handler=None` was passed to `__init__` (the
production default — every caller except tests leaves this unset), calling
`_get_agent_handler()` constructs `AgentExecutionHandler(controller=self._controller)`
fresh, not memoized, on every RUN_AGENT dispatch.

**Why incidental:** every existing test injects a fake/mock handler via the
constructor, so this line has *never executed* under test (gate: "zero test
coverage"). It is the one path that wires the real Docker-execution
collaborator. An extraction that moves `_get_agent_handler` into a new
`AgentRunCoordinator` and, say, changes the constructor arg order, renames
`controller`, or accidentally memoizes the instance, has no test that would
fail — it would only be caught in a running workspace.

**Gates:** Step 3 (extracting the RUN_AGENT handler group).

### 2.2 `_save_new_and_sync` / `_save_and_sync` divergent coverage on the same branch (865→859 vs. 868–879)

**Behaviour:** both loops fan uncommitted events out to `todo_projection.on_<snake_case>`
via `getattr(...)`, and both silently no-op when no matching handler exists.
That "no matching handler → skip" branch is exercised for `_save_and_sync`
somewhere in the suite but **not** for `_save_new_and_sync` — two copies of
one piece of logic, one tested, one not.

**Why incidental:** the two loops are ~90% identical text, not the same
tested code path. Unifying them (which the gate explicitly recommends doing
*as part of* this refactor, not after) means picking one loop's behaviour to
keep — and without a test pinning the untested copy first, "unify" could
silently promote whichever copy is easier to read, discarding the
unverified one without anyone noticing which one that was.

**Gates:** Step 1 (unifying the two sync methods) — this is the first step
for exactly this reason.

### 2.3 `_fail_execution`'s between-phases failure (473→476)

**Behaviour:** when a workflow fails with `failed_phase_id=None` (the
failure happened between phases, not inside one — e.g. a save error before
any phase started), `failed_phase_outcome(...)` returns `failed_result=None`
and `phase_results.append(failed_result)` is skipped. `phase_results` is
left exactly as it was.

**Why incidental:** every existing failure test supplies a real
`failed_phase_id` (from `dispatch_ctx.current_phase_id`), so this is a
never-taken branch, not a designed-and-tested one. An extraction that moves
`_fail_execution` into an outcome-builder and "simplifies" the `if
failed_result is not None` guard (e.g. by unwrapping the tuple return of
`failed_phase_outcome` differently) has no test that would catch appending
`None` into `phase_results`.

**Gates:** Step 6 (extracting the terminal-outcome builders).

### 2.4 `_finalize_phase`'s missing-workspace-CM branch (848→exit)

**Behaviour:** `_finalize_phase` pops `_active_workspace_cms.pop(phase_id, None)`
and only calls `await workspace_cm.__aexit__(...)` if it got a non-`None`
value. Every test that reaches finalize has a CM present, so the "already
torn down / never provisioned" case is untested.

**Why incidental:** this is a real defensive branch (not dead code — a
provisioning failure that still reaches `_finalize_phase` via a different
path could hit it), but it has zero coverage. An extraction that reorders
the pop-then-conditionally-close sequence, or that moves the four related
pops (`session_mgr`, `workspace`, `session_id`, `workspace_cm`) into a
container's own teardown method, has no test that would catch calling
`__aexit__` on `None` or skipping cleanup when the CM *is* present.

**Gates:** Step 5 (extracting COMPLETE_PHASE + `_finalize_phase`).

### 2.5 Reflection-based event serialization fallbacks (886–888)

**Behaviour:** `_serialize_event` tries `model_dump()`, then `to_dict()`,
then bare `vars(event)`, in that order. Every event that has ever flowed
through this code in practice is a Pydantic model, so branches 2 and 3 have
never executed — "dead code from the test's perspective," per the gate,
"would fail silently if it were ever not dead."

**Why incidental:** this is exactly the kind of code a refactor's diff tool
treats as an unremarkable four-line move. Moving it into a new
`TodoEventSync` collaborator with no test on the fallback order risks
silently reordering the `hasattr` checks (e.g. checking `to_dict` first) or
dropping a branch — nothing currently exercises the difference.

**Gates:** Step 2 (extracting the `TodoEventSync` collaborator).

### 2.6 The one dedicated concurrency test is the entire net for shared-instance state

**Behaviour:** `TestConcurrentFailureAttribution` (test_workflow_execution_
processor.py:405+) is the only test that proves `_DispatchContext` (created
per `run()` call, not stored on `self`) keeps `failed_phase_id` attribution
correct when two `run()` calls share one processor instance and their
dispatch is force-interleaved via an `asyncio.Event`-gated fake workspace
CM. This reproduces the exact bug the `_DispatchContext` fix addressed
(module docstring, lines 111–118).

**Why incidental:** it is thorough for the one scenario it covers
(`dispatch_ctx.current_phase_id` attribution), but the module has *ten*
other pieces of instance state shared the same way (`_active_workspaces`,
`_active_workspace_cms`, `_active_envs`, `_active_cmds`, `_session_managers`,
`_phase_session_ids`, `_phase_leader_native_ids`, `_phase_tokens`,
`_phase_auth_tokens`, `_phase_artifact_ids`, `_phase_started_at`) — none of
which have a test proving they partition correctly across concurrent
executions the way `_DispatchContext` does. If a decomposition consolidates
those ten dicts into one state container, it is trivial to pass the existing
concurrency test "by construction" (the container behaves like a dict of
dicts, so `TestConcurrentFailureAttribution` keeps passing) while silently
introducing a shared key collision in a dimension nothing tests — e.g.
keying by `phase_id` alone instead of `(execution_id, phase_id)` the way
`_phase_leader_native_ids` deliberately does today (see the docstring at
lines 184–194 explaining exactly why phase-only keys are unsafe here).

**Gates:** Step 7 (state-dict consolidation) — the last step, and only
attempted once every consumer of these dicts has already been isolated
behind a named collaborator by steps 3–6, so the swap is a mechanical,
single-seam change rather than a class-wide one.

### 2.7 A test whose name no longer matches its assertion, but whose assertion is still real

`TestProcessorTermination.test_processor_terminates_when_no_todos` — its own
docstring admits it was written for an empty-todo legacy path that no longer
exists; it now asserts that an unmocked-handler run fails at provisioning
and the processor catches the error cleanly. Not a gap to close, but a
trap: during the refactor someone will read the name, decide it's
redundant/misleading, and delete it as cleanup. **Do not.** It is currently
the only test proving the top-level `try/except` in `run()` catches a
provisioning-stage exception and routes it through `_fail_execution` rather
than propagating raw. Rename it if anything; do not remove it as part of
any step below.

## 3. Target decomposition

```
execute_workflow/
├── WorkflowExecutionProcessor.py      # __init__, run(), _drain_todo_list, _dispatch — thin, delegates
├── todo_event_sync.py                 # NEW class: TodoEventSync
├── agent_run_coordinator.py           # NEW class: AgentRunCoordinator
├── phase_provisioning_coordinator.py  # NEW class: PhaseProvisioningCoordinator
├── phase_completion_coordinator.py    # NEW class: PhaseCompletionCoordinator (collect + complete + finalize)
├── execution_outcome_builder.py       # NEW class: ExecutionOutcomeBuilder (cancel/complete/fail)
└── phase_runtime_state.py             # NEW class: PhaseRuntimeState (LAST — consolidates the 10 dicts)
```

Every "NEW class" above is a new seam, not new business logic — the
*methods* moving into it are existing, characterization-covered code
(sections 2.2–2.5 pin the parts of it that aren't already covered by the
main suite). What's genuinely new and TDD-able is:

- **The class shell itself**: constructor signature, what it's injected
  with, what its public method signature looks like. Nobody has written
  `TodoEventSync.__init__(execution_repo, todo_projection)` before — that
  contract is designed via a failing test first.
- **`PhaseRuntimeState`** (step 7): this one is new *behaviour*, not just a
  new wrapper — it has to make the `(execution_id, phase_id)` vs.
  `phase_id`-only keying decision explicit and testable per-key, which
  today lives only as a comment. TDD this one properly: write the
  concurrent-partitioning test first, watch it fail against a naive
  dict-of-dicts, then build the container to pass it.
- **`WorkflowExecutionProcessor`'s own post-refactor shape**: once it's just
  `__init__` + `run()` + `_drain_todo_list` + `_dispatch` delegating to five
  collaborators, its own wiring (which collaborator gets which dicts) is a
  new contract worth a construction-level test even though every method it
  calls is old code.

## 4. Ordering

Each step lists: the gating test(s) (must exist and pass before the
extraction lands), what moves, and what's new/TDD'd within that step. Full
existing suite must stay green after every step — that's the "stays green
throughout" requirement, checked at each step, not once at the end.

### Step 1 — Unify `_save_new_and_sync` / `_save_and_sync`

- **Gate:** one new characterization test, parametrized over both entry
  points (`is_new=True/False`), that drives a synthetic event whose
  `event_type` maps to a handler name absent from a mock `todo_projection`
  (i.e. `getattr(todo_projection, "on_whatever", None)` is `None`) through
  *both* the new-stream and normal-save paths, asserting neither raises and
  neither calls a handler. This is the only way to know both copies agree
  before merging them (§2.2). **Level: unit** — pure control flow over a
  mocked `ExecutionRepository` and a mock projection; no async I/O, no
  reason to pay for integration setup.
- **Change:** merge into one `_sync_uncommitted_events(aggregate, *,
  is_new: bool)` calling `save_new` or `save` accordingly. Still a private
  method on `WorkflowExecutionProcessor` at this point — no new file yet.
  Moved code, characterization-covered by the gate test above plus the
  existing suite (which already exercises both call sites' happy paths).
- **Verify:** full suite green + new test green.

### Step 2 — Extract `TodoEventSync`

- **Gate:** the `_serialize_event` fallback-order characterization test
  from §2.5 — three synthetic doubles (one with `model_dump`, one with only
  `to_dict`, one with neither), asserting the branch actually taken and the
  dict returned for each. **Level: unit** — pure function, three fakes, no
  I/O.
- **New (TDD first):** `TodoEventSync.__init__(execution_repository,
  todo_projection)` and `TodoEventSync.sync(aggregate, *, is_new: bool)` —
  write a failing test asserting the constructor takes exactly these two
  collaborators and `sync()` dispatches to `save_new`/`save` per the `is_new`
  flag, *before* the class exists.
- **Moved (characterization-covered):** the unified sync body from Step 1,
  `_serialize_event`, `_event_type_to_handler` — relocate unchanged; the
  Step-1 and §2.5 tests are what would catch a regression in the move.
- **Processor change:** `self._event_sync = TodoEventSync(execution_repository,
  todo_projection)`; replace both call sites with `await
  self._event_sync.sync(aggregate, is_new=...)`.
- **Verify:** full suite green + Step 1 test (now targeting the new class)
  + §2.5 test green.

### Step 3 — Extract `AgentRunCoordinator` (RUN_AGENT + cancel-signal sub-path)

- **Gate:** the `_get_agent_handler` characterization test from §2.1 — call
  it with `agent_handler=None` injected, assert the return value `isinstance(...,
  AgentExecutionHandler)` and that `.controller` is the same object passed
  to the processor's constructor. **Level: unit** — no real Docker
  execution triggered by this assertion, just object identity/type; but it
  MUST use the real `AgentExecutionHandler` class, not a mock, since the
  entire point is that this path was never constructing the real thing.
- **New (TDD first):** the coordinator's constructor contract — what it's
  injected with (a subset of the processor's collaborators:
  `conversation_storage`, `observability_writer`, `agent_handler`,
  `controller`) and its public `handle_run_agent(todo, phase, aggregate,
  ...) -> None` signature.
- **Moved (characterization-covered by existing suite + §2.1 test):**
  `_get_agent_handler`, `_handle_run_agent`, `_handle_cancel_signal`.
- **State handling:** at this point the ten ephemeral dicts still live on
  `WorkflowExecutionProcessor`. Pass the specific dicts this coordinator
  needs (`_active_workspaces`, `_active_envs`, `_active_cmds`,
  `_phase_session_ids`, `_phase_tokens`, `_phase_auth_tokens`,
  `_phase_leader_native_ids`, `_phase_started_at`) into its constructor **by
  reference** — same physical dict objects, still owned and shared by the
  one processor instance, so the concurrency contract from §2.6 is
  unchanged (nothing about *where the reference lives* changes who reads
  and writes it, or when). Do not copy these dicts.
- **Verify:** full suite green (including `TestConcurrentFailureAttribution`,
  which exercises this exact path) + §2.1 test green.

### Step 4 — Extract `PhaseProvisioningCoordinator` (PROVISION_WORKSPACE)

- **Gate:** none new — `_handle_provision` / `_provision_workspace`'s
  happy path and the stale-workspace defensive branch it feeds
  (`_handle_collect_artifacts`'s `workspace is None` check, itself already
  covered by `test_workflow_execution_processor.py`) are both exercised by
  the existing suite. No named incidental gap here per the coverage gate's
  report, so this step relies entirely on the existing suite as its net.
- **New (TDD first):** constructor contract (`workspace_service,
  prompt_builder, command_builder, claude_plugin_materializer,
  skill_materializer, session_repository, observability_writer,
  artifact_repository, artifact_content_storage, artifact_query`) and
  public `handle_provision(...)`.
- **Moved:** `_handle_provision`, `_provision_workspace`, by reference to
  `_active_workspaces`, `_active_workspace_cms`, `_active_envs`,
  `_active_cmds`, `_session_managers`, `_phase_started_at`.
- **Verify:** full suite green.

### Step 5 — Extract `PhaseCompletionCoordinator` (COLLECT_ARTIFACTS + COMPLETE_PHASE + `_finalize_phase`)

- **Gate:** the `_finalize_phase` missing-CM characterization test from
  §2.4 — call `_finalize_phase` (or, once moved, the coordinator's
  equivalent) directly with no entry in `_active_workspace_cms` for the
  phase, assert no exception and no `__aexit__` call recorded on a spy.
  **Level: unit** — the method under test is already a private async
  method taking explicit args; no need for the full `run()` loop.
- **New (TDD first):** constructor contract and public
  `handle_collect_artifacts(...)` / `handle_complete_phase(...)` signatures.
- **Moved:** `_handle_collect_artifacts`, `_handle_complete_phase`,
  `_finalize_phase`, by reference to `_active_workspaces`,
  `_active_workspace_cms`, `_active_envs`, `_active_cmds`,
  `_session_managers`, `_phase_session_ids`, `_phase_leader_native_ids`,
  `_phase_tokens`, `_phase_auth_tokens`, `_phase_artifact_ids`,
  `_phase_started_at`.
- **Verify:** full suite green (`test_capture_before_teardown.py` is the
  ordering-sensitive net here — capture-before-teardown is exactly the
  invariant this coordinator must not reorder) + §2.4 test green.

### Step 6 — Extract `ExecutionOutcomeBuilder` (cancel / complete / fail + `_close_phase_workspace_cms`)

- **Gate:** the between-phases-failure characterization test from §2.3 —
  call `_fail_execution` (or its post-move equivalent) with
  `failed_phase_id=None` and a `failed_phase_outcome` double returning
  `(duration, None)`, assert `phase_results` is unchanged (same length,
  same identity) after the call. **Level: unit** — the function under test
  already takes `phase_results: list[PhaseResult]` as an explicit
  mutable-append target; a mock aggregate and mock session managers are
  enough, no real workspace or Docker needed.
- **New (TDD first):** constructor contract and public
  `build_cancelled(...)` / `build_completed(...)` / `build_failed(...)`
  signatures.
- **Moved:** `_cancel_execution`, `_complete_execution`, `_fail_execution`,
  `_close_phase_workspace_cms`, by reference to `_session_managers`,
  `_active_workspace_cms`, `_active_workspaces`, `_active_envs`,
  `_active_cmds`, `_phase_session_ids`, `_phase_leader_native_ids`,
  `_phase_started_at`.
- **Verify:** full suite green (`TestProcessorCancellation` and
  `TestConcurrentFailureAttribution` are the two tests that most directly
  exercise this move — both assert exact post-call dict state, so a
  reference-vs-copy mistake in this extraction fails loudly) + §2.3 test
  green + §2.7's test still present and green under its current name or a
  renamed one.

### Step 7 — Consolidate the ten ephemeral dicts into `PhaseRuntimeState` (last, and only if still needed)

Only attempt this if `WorkflowExecutionProcessor` is still over 750 lines
after steps 1–6, or if the ten-dict `__init__` block is judged worth
collapsing on its own merits. It is the highest-risk step in this plan and
every consumer of the dicts has, by this point, already been isolated
behind the four coordinators above — so this becomes "swap what those four
constructors are given," not a class-wide change.

- **Gate:** extend `TestConcurrentFailureAttribution` (do not write a
  parallel test — extend the existing one, since it already has the
  `asyncio.Event`-gated interleave machinery this needs) to also assert,
  after the forced interleave, that a `PhaseRuntimeState` container built
  with the same `phase_id` used by both concurrent executions produces
  distinct values per `(execution_id, phase_id)` for at least one dict that
  is keyed that way today (`_phase_leader_native_ids`), and per `phase_id`
  alone for one that is deliberately keyed that way (matching current
  behaviour — do not "fix" the keying scheme during this move; that's a
  behaviour change, not a decomposition, and belongs in its own PR if
  wanted). **Level: integration** — this is the one gate in this whole plan
  that cannot be unit-tested: the entire point is proving the *interleave*
  behaves correctly under real `asyncio` scheduling, which is exactly what
  `TestConcurrentFailureAttribution`'s fake gated workspace CM exists to
  force. A mocked/serial call sequence would pass regardless of whether the
  container partitions correctly, so it would validate nothing.
- **New, TDD from a failing version of the extended test above:**
  `PhaseRuntimeState` — write the extended concurrency test against a naive
  first implementation, watch it fail (e.g. because a naive
  implementation defaults everything to phase-id-only keying), then build
  the container's actual key scheme to pass it, per dict.
- **Moved:** nothing code-wise moves here — the four coordinators from
  steps 3–6 change from taking eight separate dict references to taking one
  `PhaseRuntimeState` reference. Their own logic is untouched.
- **Verify:** full suite green + extended concurrency test green.

## 5. Summary: TDD vs. characterization, per artifact

| Artifact | Discipline | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Unified `_sync_uncommitted_events` body | Characterization (Step 1 test) | Existing logic, existing behaviour, just deduplicated |
| `TodoEventSync` class shell (ctor, `sync()` signature) | TDD | Contract never existed before |
| `TodoEventSync`'s moved body (`_serialize_event`, `_event_type_to_handler`) | Characterization (§2.5 test + existing suite) | Existing logic |
| `AgentRunCoordinator` shell | TDD | New contract |
| `AgentRunCoordinator`'s moved body | Characterization (§2.1 test + existing suite, esp. `TestConcurrentFailureAttribution`) | Existing logic |
| `PhaseProvisioningCoordinator` shell | TDD | New contract |
| `PhaseProvisioningCoordinator`'s moved body | Characterization (existing suite only — no named gap) | Existing logic |
| `PhaseCompletionCoordinator` shell | TDD | New contract |
| `PhaseCompletionCoordinator`'s moved body | Characterization (§2.4 test + `test_capture_before_teardown.py`) | Existing logic |
| `ExecutionOutcomeBuilder` shell | TDD | New contract |
| `ExecutionOutcomeBuilder`'s moved body | Characterization (§2.3 test + `TestProcessorCancellation`, `TestConcurrentFailureAttribution`) | Existing logic |
| `PhaseRuntimeState` (keying behaviour itself) | TDD, from a failing extended concurrency test | Genuinely new behaviour — the keying scheme is currently a comment, not a tested contract |
| Post-refactor `WorkflowExecutionProcessor` (thin `run`/`_dispatch` + wiring) | TDD for the wiring, characterization (full suite) for `run`/`_drain_todo_list`/`_dispatch` bodies | The bodies are unchanged; which collaborator gets constructed with what is a new, checkable decision |

## 6. What this plan deliberately does not do

- Does not change the reflection-based `getattr(todo_projection, "on_<snake>")`
  dispatch mechanism, the phase-only vs. `(execution_id, phase_id)` keying
  split across the ten state dicts, or fix the `_serialize_event` dead
  fallback branches. Those are behaviour changes the coverage gate flagged
  as residual risk to *close*, and this plan closes the *coverage* gap on
  each (so a future behaviour change would have a net) without changing
  the behaviour itself. Fixing them is separate work.
- Does not touch `phase_outcome.py`, `phase_delegate_import.py`,
  `phase_conversation.py`, `ArtifactCollector.py`, `SessionLifecycleManager.py`,
  or any of the three infrastructure handlers (`WorkspaceProvisionHandler`,
  `AgentExecutionHandler`, `ArtifactCollectionHandler`) — those are already
  separate files this processor calls into; nothing here changes.
- Does not touch `_DispatchContext` — it is already correctly scoped
  per-`run()`-call (not instance state), and is the existing model §2.6 and
  Step 7 hold up as what "moved into a new container but stayed
  interleave-safe" should look like.
